_comment: Thresholds and the never-touch list. quarantine.ps1 enforces never_touch in code - it is not advisory. Edit values here rather than in scripts.

caps._comment: A single run refusing to exceed these is the runaway guard. Excess is downgraded to Holding in the report rather than staged.

downloads._comment: Only these extensions are quarantine-eligible in Downloads. Everything else is report-only - a stale .docx may still be the only copy of something.

dev_artifacts._comment: Directory names treated as regenerable build output. Eligible only when the parent project's newest source file is older than dev_artifact_age_days.

system_caches._comment: Quarantine-eligible regenerable caches. Browser profile data is deliberately absent - clearing it destroys logged-in sessions, which is a privacy action, not a space action.

never_touch._comment: Enforced inside quarantine.ps1. Any candidate resolving under one of these prefixes is dropped with a logged reason, regardless of what any scan proposed.
never_touch._comment_names: Path segments that disqualify a candidate anywhere in its path. .git and .ssh protect repo history and keys; Agency protects this bot and its siblings, notably finance-research/.venv which matches the dev-artifact pattern but is live infrastructure. 'claude' and '.claude' protect Claude Code's own scratchpad, task output and config - %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\claude sits inside a scanned cache path, so without this the bot stages the session state of whatever Claude run is happening at the time, including its own.
never_touch._comment_files: System files whose deletion breaks or destabilises Windows.

report_only._comment: Surfaced in the report with sizes and a suggested command, never acted on. Uninstalls are permanently here - 'do I still use this?' is a human judgement, and games are the largest category on this machine by a wide margin.
